entities.text:
Mamidi Shankar, Warangal Dist And 13 ... vs Deputy Collector,
Warangal Dist
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This writ petition is filed seeking to declare the action of the respondents in not referring the claim of the petitioners to a Civil Court under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act') as illegal and arbitrary and direct the respondents forthwith to refer the claims of the petitioners to a Civil Court under Section 18 of the Act.

2. Learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are owners and possessors of different extents of the agricultural lands situated at Ashireddypally Village of Chityal Mandal,
Warangal District.
The said lands were acquired by the Government for the purpose of excavation of Kakatiya Canal in the year, 1990, Award was passed and the petitioners were also paid compensation.

Learned Counsel submits that though the petitioners SK,J made representations on 21.03.2001 and 12.01.2009 seeking reference to a Civil Court for proper adjudication of the compensation, no action has been taken by the respondents, which is illegal and arbitrary and requested to allow the writ petition.

3. Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for the respondent No.1 based on the counter averments submits that pursuant to the requisition for acquisition of certain lands for excavation of canal, the Special Collector, L.A, Hyderabad has approved DN proposals and PV proposals by fixing the market value @ Rs.30,000/- per acre for dry lands covered under acquisition.
Thereafter, enquiry was conducted and an Award was passed on 14.02.2001.

Out of 43 awardees, 42 awardees have received compensation and filed petitions under Section 18 of the Act on 21.03.2001 stating that the acquired lands are fertile lands with capacity of raising commercial crops i.e., cotton and SK,J chillies and they are getting average annual income of Rs.5,000/- on yield and the value of the lands under acquisition is not less than Rs.1,00,000/- per acre to Rs.1,30,000/-
per acre and as the value fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer at Rs.30,000/- is very low, they requested to refer the said petition to the Civil Court for proper adjudication.
Out of 42 petitions

,
only 27 petitions were referred to the Civil Court and the remaining 15 petitions were rejected by the then Land Acquisition Officer on the ground that the said awardees have received the compensation amount awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer vide award dated 14.02.2001 without protesting the compensation amount while taking it in Form-CC and Acquaintance Register.
Mamidi Shankar, Warangal Dist And 13 ... vs Deputy Collector, Warangal Dist And ... on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193901799/

1 4. Learned Government Pleader further submits that if the petitioners file petitions for reference within the specified time as per Section 18 of the Act, the SK,J respondents will consider the same in accordance with law.

5. Having heard both sides and perusal of the record, this Court is of the considered view that the petitioners have admitted about receiving of compensation amount awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer vide award dated 14.02.2001.

As per the averments in the counter affidavit, out of 43 awardees, 42 awardees have received compensation and filed petitions on 21.03.2001 under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act seeking reference to the Civil Court for enhancement of the compensation and out of 42 petitions, only 27 petitions were referred and the petitions filed by the petitioners were rejected on the ground that they have received compensation without protesting the amount while taking it in the Form-CC and Acquittance Register.

SK,J 6. Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 reads as under;
"Reference to Court:-(1) Any person interested who has not accepted the award may,
by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Court, whether his objection be to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the persons to whom it is payable, or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested.
(2) The application shall state the grounds on which objection to the award is taken:
Provided that every such application shall be made- (a) if the person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, within six weeks from the date of the Collector's award;
(b) in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under Section 12 sub-section (2), or within six months from the date of the Collector's award, whichever period shall first expire."
As per Section 18 of the Act, the persons who are aggrieved by the compensation may file written application to the Collector stating the grounds on which objection to the award is taken and such application shall be made within six weeks from the SK,J date of the Collector's award.

In the instant case, the award was passed on 14.02.2001 and the petitioners filed representation/petition on 21.03.2001 i.e, within six weeks as stipulated in Section 18 of the Act and the matter has to be referred to the Civil Court for determination.

7. The contention of the respondents that the petitioners have received compensation without protesting the amount while taking it in the Form-CC and Acquaintance Register is not tenable because no such clause is mentioned in Section 18 of the Act with regard to rejection of the petitions Mamidi Shankar, Warangal Dist And 13 ... vs Deputy Collector, Warangal Dist And ... on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193901799/
2 filed for reference to Court.
8.

sentences.text:
In the above facts and circumstances, the Writ Petition is allowed directing the respondents to refer the claim of the petitioners to the Civil Court under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894 within SK,J eight (8) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
No order as to costs.
9. Miscellaneous Applications, if any pending in this writ petition, shall stand closed.
